newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-CARSON TO RIDE AGAIN AFTER ACCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CARSON TO RIDE AGAIN AFTER ACCIDENT.

text.p: Veteran jockey Willie Carson, recovering from a horrific riding accident that threatened to end his career, said on Wednesday he aims to be back in the saddle next season.
"I hope to be back for the start of the racing season in March," the 53-year-old Scotsman told a television interviewer.

Carson was flung into the air by a kick in the stomach from his mount at Newbury in September. His liver was seriously damaged but the protective chest pad he was wearing saved him from even worse injuries.
"I just remember putting my hand up to grab the rein and then the next thing is her backside is touching my nose and then bang. Then I remember being in a lot of pain," he said.
"When I put my hand out to get hold of the reins, I saw her eye and I thought `I want out of here' but she jumped forward and wham."
Carson said doctors had warned him not to even think about riding competitively until the end of this year. "I have to get back in the gym and then see what happens," he said.
